question:
A 34-year-old gravida 3, para 2 woman at approximately 8 weeks of gestation presents with a 3-day
history of intermittent vaginal spotting. She denies fever, chills, cramping, or abnormal vaginal
discharge. A pelvic ultrasound reveals a mean gestational sac diameter of 17 mm with no visible
embryo. Her serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin level was 1950 mIU/mL two days ago and has
decreased to 1898 mIU/mL today. The patient is tearful, as she strongly desires this pregnancy. What
is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Perform serial beta human
chorionic gonadotropin measurements over 48 hours (B) Repeat the ultrasound in one week (C)
Perform dilation and curettage immediately (D) Initiate methotrexate therapy for ectopic pregnancy (E)
Prescribe progesterone supplementation (F) Refer for surgical management of miscarriage (G)
Prescribe one dose of misoprostol (H) Perform a repeat ultrasound within 48 hours (I) Measure the
beta human chorionic gonadotropin level in 24 hours (J) Advise expectant management without further
testing
 A. Measure the beta human chorionic gonadotropin level in 24 hours
B. Perform serial beta human chorionic gonadotropin measurements over 48 hours
C. Prescribe progesterone supplementation
D. Prescribe one dose of misoprostol
E. Initiate methotrexate therapy for ectopic pregnancy
F. Perform a repeat ultrasound within 48 hours
G. Repeat the ultrasound in one week
H. Perform dilation and curettage immediately
I. Advise expectant management without further testing
J. Refer for surgical management of miscarriage
